title: Cloud Agents and Automations
description:
In this workshop, we cover how to move from in-editor help to cloud agents and automations.

Key workflows covered:

Maturity curve:

Move from on-the-shoulder help to background cloud agents, then to an AI software factory where automations carry work from idea to done with light review.

Sync foundation:

Use Ask Mode to explore a repo and Design Mode to edit selected UI in the browser. Commit skills and use subagents for repeatable work like test coverage.

Cloud agents:

Run larger tasks in isolated cloud VMs, then review screenshots, recordings, or pull requests later. There is no separate hosting fee. Usage is billed on tokens.

Automations:

Tie an agent to a trigger, like a Slack bug report, so it investigates, fixes, verifies, and keeps memory for the next run.

Guardrails:

Use hooks and worktrees to check async work and avoid collisions. poteto-mode, from the pstack plugin, runs a heavier plan-and-verify loop.

title: How AI Agents are Rewiring the SDLC
description:
In this workshop, we cover how agents can plan, build, review, and recover across the SDLC.

Key workflows covered:

Plan and design:

Use Plan Mode to write a spec with requirements, tests, and steps for the next agent. You can also start from a Jira or Linear ticket and pull context from Slack or Confluence.

Build:

Keep short rules and skills so agents follow your repo's practices. Build on the IDE, CLI, or Agents Window, with rules always on and skills applied only when relevant.

Test and review:

Run Bugbot and Security Reviewer on every pull request. Bugbot can autofix low-severity issues and leave medium and high ones for an engineer.

Monitor:

Trigger a cloud agent from PagerDuty to pull Datadog, recent commits, and triage the incident before you sit down to debug.

Playbooks:

Start small with a Slack trigger that opens a pull request. Then chain small skill-shaped agents the way Benny does for bug triage.

title: Measuring Developer Productivity in Code Review
description:
In this workshop, AJ Valenty and Pat Wolfe (Forward Deployed Engineering / Origin) dig into how code review is changing in the age of agentic coding - and how to measure developer productivity when AI is writing more of the code.

Drawing on Cursor's Developer Habits report, they cover what's shifted over the past year: developers are shipping far more code, pull requests are getting much larger, and more changes are being accepted without a manual line-by-line review. The bottleneck moves downstream to review and testing - creating PR backlogs, overwhelmed senior engineers, rubber-stamp reviews, and even source-control infrastructure straining under agent-driven volume.

They walk through Cursor's two-layer review approach:

Agentic review: bots that review PRs immediately at a senior-level bar

Bugbot - logic, syntax, and style, with org-wide context

Security reviewer - catches vulnerabilities before merge

Approver / router - routes PRs and can auto-approve low-risk changes

Vulnerability scanner - scheduled scans that open PRs and pipe findings into Slack

Human review: freed up for higher-level architectural concerns

Also covered: Cursor automations, cloud agents, and the Cursor SDK - plus the ROI metrics Cursor uses to evaluate review tooling.

title: The Outer Loop: Code Reviews in Cursor
description:
In this workshop, Tomas Reimers covers how agentic software development is reshaping the outer loop of code review.

Key trends covered:

Agentic reviews:

AI reviewers leave comments on PRs. Teams are moving from one omniscient bot to specialized reviewers (bugs, security) owned by different orgs.

Agentic approvals:

Low-risk PRs can be auto-approved. Higher-risk changes get the best human reviewers assigned automatically.

Agentic iteration:

Authors hand off comment resolution and meaningful PR edits to agents, not just one-off @mentions for tiny fixes.

Year of async:

More agents run in the background and ping developers, so work continues outside a live IDE session.

Bugbot \& Origin:

How Cursor's review bot and GitHub alternative fit agent-era PR volume and workflows.

Audit logs \& receipts:

Even with agents in the loop, outer-loop work still needs a durable record of what changed and why.

title: power-user workflows from local agents to cloud fleets and automations.
description:
In this workshop, we cover power-user workflows from local agents to cloud fleets and automations.

Key workflows covered:

Agents window \& surfaces:

Manage local and cloud agents across repos from one pane. Use workspaces for multi-repo front-end and back-end work.

Ask → Plan → Build:

Start in Ask mode to orient in the codebase. Switch to Plan mode for an editable plan, then execute with Composer 2.5.

Subagents \& Multitask:

Subagents delegate work in isolated context windows with their own models. Multitask lets you define parallel tasks in one session.

Cloud agents \& skills:

Hand off long-running features to cloud agents with computer use. Monitor runs from desktop, web, or phone using repo skills.

Skills, Marketplace \& automations:

Package repeatable workflows as skills and share plugins via Marketplace. Trigger Jira-to-PR automations with webhooks and Slack updates.

title: How to select the right model for the right task
description:
In this workshop, we cover how to select the right AI model for the right task and how to optimize token usage to get better results while spending less.

Key topics covered:

Token basics:

\~4 characters per token. Input is the silent cost because it compounds with every agent loop.

Model selection:

Match the model to the task. Composer is purpose-built for coding at a fraction of the cost (\~$0.55 vs \~$11 per task for Opus 4.8).

Plan the shot:

A specific prompt with clear success criteria can reduce token usage by 5x. Vague prompts send agents exploring.

Plan Mode:

Plan with a general reasoning model, then execute with Composer.

Context management:

Start a new chat per task. Audit your rules and MCP tools since they load every loop. Prefer skills over rules.

View Report:

Click the % ring under the prompt box to inspect exactly what's consuming your context window.

title: Cursor Automations
description:
In this workshop, we build Cursor Automations - cloud agents triggered by events or schedules to automate the software development lifecycle.

Topics covered:

Automations \& agent teammates:

Automations let you build a fleet of agent teammates running on cloud agents (Cursor-hosted or self-hosted VMs) to automate SDLC toil like bug triage, feature-flag cleanup, and reviews.

Anatomy of an automation:

Each automation has a repo (single or multi), a trigger like a Slack message, schedule, or PR, a system prompt, a model, and tools such as Jira and Slack.

Version control with skills:

Codify the core of each automation as a skill in your .cursor folder for version control. Run history, success and failure counts, and audit logs help you debug and tune them.

Productized automations:

Beyond custom ones, BugBot reviews PRs and can autofix by spinning up a cloud agent, while Security Review gives risk scores, configurable at the PR, repo, or org level.

Repo-less automations:

Automations can run without a codebase as general-purpose agents - daily industry briefs, after-hours Slack digests, or even image generation.

title: Securing Agent Outputs
description:
In this workshop, we explore how to keep agent-generated code safe at PR review and at runtime.

Key workflows covered:

Bugbot PR Reviews: Bugbot reviews pull requests for risky patterns and enforces rules around eval, exec, and questionable OSS licenses before code merges.

Bugbot Dashboard: Set Bugbot effort levels, apply one-click autofixes, and monitor findings with analytics from the Bugbot dashboard.

Hooks: Attach deterministic scripts at trigger points like file write, prompt submit, and MCP calls to enforce compliance and capture telemetry.

Sandbox Mode: Bound terminal access with command allowlists so agents operate within defined security limits.

Audit Logs \& Privacy Mode: Audit Logs give visibility into agent activity, while Privacy Mode keeps your code out of model training and retention.

title: customize Cursor Agent with rules, skills, MCP servers, hooks, and the marketplace.
description:
In this workshop, we cover how to customize Cursor Agent with rules, skills, MCP servers, hooks, and the marketplace.

Key features covered:

Rules: Encode your team's standards and inject persistent context. Use always, intelligent, glob, or manual triggers, and keep always-apply rules lean to protect the context window.

Skills: Bundle reusable workflows the agent fetches dynamically or you call as commands. Skills are shared across .cursor, .cloud, and .codex folders, so they carry over between agents.

MCP servers: Connect Cursor to external tools like Linear, Jira, and Figma. Tools load dynamically, so relevant context comes in without leaving the editor.

Hooks: Enforce deterministic controls at trigger points like prompt submit. Command-based and prompt-based hooks handle audit logging and secret scanning across the agent loop.

Marketplace: Install or publish plugins that bundle rules, skills, subagents, commands, hooks, and MCP servers into one package for your team.

title: How AI Agents are Rewiring the SDLC
description:
In this workshop, we cover how AI agents reshape the software development lifecycle in Cursor.

Key topics:

Agents across the SDLC: See how agents augment planning, design, development, testing, and deployment instead of only codegen.

Workflow and ownership: Learn what changes in tooling, rituals, and accountability when agents are active participants.

Incremental adoption: Use practical patterns to roll agents out without disrupting existing processes.

Planning and scope: Scope work in Plan Mode so agents align on specs before they edit your codebase.

Build and deliver: Use IDE and cloud agents to implement changes and open PRs across the lifecycle.

Review at scale: Understand why review becomes the bottleneck as velocity rises, and how agent review helps.

title: Panel Charts in Excel
description: Divide your chart into separate panels for different data. Prevent confusion due to overlapping dual-axis data. Split stacked chart data into separate mini-charts. This session will demonstrate two examples of this technique, while also showing several useful charting tricks. Jon Peltier is a master of leveraging the power of Excel to produce and simplify complex solutions in engineering, finance, and marketing. Jon holds a Doctor of Science degree from MIT in Metallurgy, his background includes Manufacturing, Statistics, Total Quality, and Six Sigma. Jon programs extensively in VBA to improve user productivity and allow faster analysis and display of data, and he knows more about Excel charts than practically anyone. Jon has been a full time Excel developer since 2004, and has received Microsoft's Most Valuable Professional award every year since 2001.

title: Customizing Excel to improve efficiency
description: This session will cover some easy, but often under-used ways that you can customize Excel to save yourself from repeating tasks. Setting up default templates for new workbooks and worksheets can be a great time-saver, and this session will show you how to use them to your advantage. Cell Styles are a great way to add consistency and flexibility to your workbooks. I'll show how to set them up and give you some great examples that you can start using right away. VBA is still alive and well, and I'll provide examples of how to use the Personal Macro Workbook to automate common tasks. Steve Kraynak is a Microsoft MVP, recognized for his expertise and contributions to the community of Excel users worldwide. He is a Director of SumProduct US, LLC, a leading modelling, training, and business consulting firm, with offices around the world.

title: Building Forecast Models with AI, Excel, and Trial & Error
description: This session will compare and contrast how far ChatGPT and Copilot have come in getting data, challenging it, forecasting it and performing scenario analyses using both charting tools and Excel. It highlights things to look out for, the importance of prompt engineering and checking your answers!! Liam Bastick is Managing Director of SumProduct, a Fellow of three accounting institute, 14x Excel MVP and holder of the inaugural Lifetime Achievement Award for Financial Modelling (FMI, 2021). He writes regularly in the accounting press and has written over 10 books, including Introduction to Financial Modelling, Financial Modelling in Power BI, Financial Modelling using Dynamic Arrays and the upcoming Financial Modelling using AI. Worst of all is his sense of humour: you have been warned!

title: Extraer + Analizar + Automatizar = Excel
description: Extraemos información de 100 facturas, analizamos el contenido y automatizaciones el proceso de renombrar las facturas. Sergio Alejandro Campos es MVP de Excel, CEO de Deztaca y EXCELeINFO. Creador de contenido para YouTube y todas las plataformas sociales. Profesor de la Certificación Excel Expert.

title: Building RAG Solutions with Azure AI Foundry
description: This session will guide you through the process of building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solution using Azure AI Foundry. 活动简介
Semantic Kernel 是微软发布的一个轻量级的开源开发工具包，旨在帮助开发者轻松构建 AI 代理并将最新的 AI 模型集成到 C#、Python 或 Java 代码库中。它作为一种高效的中间件，特别适用于构建智能助手、智能客服和自然语言交互系统等应用，为用户和企业提供更加智能和高效的解决方案。
随着全球科技浪潮的汹涌澎湃，人工智能作为引领未来的战略性技术，正以前所未有的速度重塑着世界经济的版图。在此背景下，12月10-11日即将举行的2024年全球人工智能产品应用博览会（AIExpo2024）以“以智提质，向新而行”为主题，聚焦生成式AI、具身机器人、工业AI、智能计算、跨境合作等领域，将举办高规格开幕式&主论坛、特色主题论坛、创新创业大赛、供需对接会、新品发布、互动展示等同期活动，汇聚全球智慧与创新力量，旨在探索人工智能技术的无限可能，推动产业深度融合与转型升级。
作为这一国际性盛会的重要组成部分，12月11日，开启企业全智能化应用场景 -- Semantic Kernel 开发者日中国站，来自开源 AI 领域的技术专家、业务专家，将围绕 Semantic Kernel，为现场观众带来在线教育平台、企业智能助手、智能客服系统、大模型集成等领域的应用案例分享，以及动手实践工作坊，帮助开发者快速上手 Semantic Kernel，部署适应自己的 AI 模型，并进一步赋能企业全智能化应用场景。

title: Semantic Kernel 开发者日 [9]
description:

在 Microsoft Build 2023 ，Copilot Stack 的提出，让大模型应用在企业中落地有了很好的方法论。而在 Copilot Stack 中对标的开源框架是 Semantic Kernel ，通过 Semantic Kernel 你可以打通代码与 Prompt 之间的联系外，也可以用 Planner 更有效地规划好人机对话方式，让企业可以快速融入智能化应用。Semantic Kernel 在中国有非常多的用户，不仅有传统的 .NET 开发者，也有 Python 开发者，以及 Java 开发者。Semantic Kernel 结合主流的编程语言为企业级别的 Copilot 应用保驾护航。9月23日，我们会在 Microsoft Reactor 上海联同微软最有价值专家，社区技术大拿，以及行业专家一起成立 Semantic Kernel 技术社区，并开启一天的 Semantic Kernel 开发者日。

title: Let's Learn .NET｜通过 Semantic Kernel .NET SDK 管理你的 OpenAI 项目
description:
活动主题：Let's Learn .NET｜通过 Semantic Kernel .NET SDK 管理你的 OpenAI 项目

「 “Let's Learn .NET” 是面向全球的 .NET 初学者学习系列，旨在通过不同语言，帮助不同地区的开发者掌握最新的 .NET 开发知识与技能。」

在 ChatGPT 与 OpenAI 火热的当下，“面向 AI 编程”已经成为各技术领域的开发者们关注与探索的方向。.NET 自然也不例外。

3月17日，微软宣布了轻量级 SDK -- Semantic Kernel，它提供了开箱即用的模板、链接与规划功能，允许你轻松地将传统编程语言（如 C# 和 Python）与最新的大型语言模型（LLM）AI “提示”相结合，从而更快地构建 AI 优先的应用程序。借助 Semantic Kernel，.NET 开发者也可以轻松实现面向 OpenAI 编程。

本期“Let's Learn .NET”，我们将一起学习什么是 Semantic Kernel，以及如何通过 Semantic Kernel .NET SDK 管理你的 OpenAI 项目。

title: Getting Started with JavaScript
description:
If you want to start programming for the web, one language you’ll need to have in your toolbelt is JavaScript. JavaScript is the industry standard for web development. With the use of JavaScript, you can make your pages dynamic and interactive. In this workshop recording, we walk through the core syntax and functionality. Then, we learn about libraries and frameworks which can help make your life as a developer easier. 

Speaker: Dana L. Wyatt 

Dana has a bachelor's, master's and Ph.D. degree in Computer Science. She has spent the last 25+ years as a technical trainer. Her recent work involves helping people learn about topics such as: C#/VB, Xamarin, WinForms, WPF, ASP.NET WebForms, ASP.NET MVC, Swift, Objective-C, C/C++, HTML5/CSS/Bootstrap, JavaScript, jQuery, Angular, SQL, UML, and design patterns. Prior to her career as a technical trainer, Dr. Wyatt spent 13 years on the Computer Science faculties at the University of North Texas, Texas Christian University and Texas A&M University where she taught classes in programming languages, database systems, simulation techniques, operating systems, computer architecture, and problem solving. title: Simplify development with Microsoft Graph, a chat with Beth Pan | Web Wednesday
description:
The Microsoft Graph Toolkit is a group of reusable, *framework-agnostic* components and authentication providers for working with Microsoft Graph. You can add components to existing applications, and work in any modern browser.

What is the session about? 
Web development can be challenging and sometimes might feel a little overwhelming. There are so many different technologies, emerging languages, and plug-ins that it can be hard to keep up. We’ve decide to break it down for you week by week in our Web Wednesday Interview show. This week we'll be talking to Beth Pan about the Microsoft Graph Toolkit. The Microsoft Graph Toolkit is a group of reusable, *framework-agnostic* components and authentication providers for working with Microsoft Graph. You can add components to existing applications, and work in any modern browser. Join us as we chat with Beth Pan about the toolkit, and how you can incorporate otherwise complex functionality, including authentication, with just a few lines of code.

Who is it aimed at? 
This show is for anyone who is interested in Web Development and wants to talk about what's new and exciting in the world of web development!

Why should you attend?
Each week we'll bring on people from the product teams and experts in different areas of web development. They'll talk about their own personal experiences, and reply to your questions about various topics. This week, Beth will show us how we can simplify complex functions with just a few lines of code using the toolkit!

Presenter:
Christopher Harrison, Senior Program Manager, Microsoft 
Christopher is a longtime web dev who turned a coding hobby into a career. Currently a Senior Program Manager at Microsoft, he never lost the joy he felt in writing code and having the computer do what he asked and sharing that passion with others. These days he can be found at a keyboard writing TypeScript and Python. When not at a keyboard he can be found running long distances or relaxing with his wife and their four-legged child (an adorable dog) in Seattle.

Beth Pan, Software Engineer, Microsoft 
Beth Pan is a software engineer with Microsoft. She works with first and third party developer ecosystems and help them unblock in order to build on top of Microsoft technologies and platforms. Currently she’s working on the Microsoft Graph Toolkit team to make it easier for developers to integrate their apps with Microsoft Graph. A grad of THE Ohio State University, Beth loves college football, her puppy and boyfriend - probably in that order.

This session will explore how to build lists and how to surface them in Teams

Who is it aimed at?
End Users, Power Users, Administrators

Why should I attend? 
Come and learn about how Microsoft Lists works inside Microsoft Teams and how your Team can track and organise their work by building and collaborating on rich lists which cover a range of business scenarios

Additional Learning: https://aka.ms/EngageEmployeeswithStreamTeamsYammer-11

title: Azure Overview
description:
O Azure é uma plataforma que oferece vários serviços para que as pessoas e organizações de todo o mundo possam alcançar mais .

Por que assistir esta sessão?
Uma visão geral do que é o Azure e como ele pode solucionar alguns problemas comuns em empresas.

 Aprenda mais sobre este assunto ao completar os roteiros de aprendizagens no Microsoft Learn: https://docs.microsoft.com/pt-br/users/microsoftazuretrainingandcertifications/collections/m6d0hn5nn3edn3

- Fabiano Jamati (MTC Azure Architect)
Fabiano Jamati é um apaixonado por tecnologia e acredita que ela possa mudar o mundo para melhor. Com quase 20 anos de experiencia em TI e passem por grandes empresas da área. Atualmente ocupa a vaga de Arquiteto de Azure no MTC (Microsoft Technology Center)
https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabianojamati/

 Sobre os eventos MTC Experience:
O MTC Experience é uma iniciativa em parceria com Microsoft Technology Center que compartilha com a comunidade novidades relacionadas as três nuvens da Microsoft: Business Aplications, Modern Workplace e o Azure. Todo mês, vamos apresentar conteúdos técnicos que já foram promovidos em alguns dos 40 Microsoft Technical Centers espalhados pelo mundo para grandes empresas.

Código do Evento: 12896

title: Industrial IoT - Connect your Edge to the Plant Floor
description:
Azure IoT Edge allows Windows and Linux devices to be deployed in remote locations with sporadic connectivity allowing for localized data capture and processing of events from sensors and control networks. When it comes to the plant floor there are numerous complexities involved in connecting to physical devices whether a CNC controller, programmable logic control (PLC) or sensor networks such as ModBus or DeviceNet. This complexity introduces challenges when it comes to integrating these devices with cloud services to extend additional insight and provide business value to our customers.

What is this session about:
This session will walk through the Industrial IoT capabilities of IoT Edge that makes it easier for controls and process engineers to integrate their plant floor devices with IoT Edge and be centrally managed by Azure IoT services.
Speaker: Ryan Berry, Cloud Solutions Architect, Microsoft

Ryan has over 20 years of application development experience working in technical leadership, architecture, development and support delivery roles helping customers, partners and ISVs envision and progress innovative ideas into functioning applications solving real world business and engineering challenges. From line of business applications running mission critical Enterprise workloads to time sensitive real-time software running robots and lasers on the plant floor, Ryan’s background in development has spanned across many verticals, technologies and platforms.
Ryan has been at Microsoft over 14 years in many different roles in Microsoft services, consulting, support and most recently helping Enterprise customers across the US understand how to leverage cloud computing effectively as a Cloud Solution architect.

title: Before First Lines Of Code | Learn with Dr G
description:
Want to make a game but have no idea on how to get started? Feel overwhelmed about what tool or engine to use to bring your idea to life? Can’t draw anything but a stick figure, or don’t know what questions you should be asking? Join us for a live session with special guest to walk you through the early stages of game development before your first line of code. 

You’ll leave this session with tips, tools and recommendations on how to structure and build a game that will meet it’s intended design goals.

title: Create Power Apps in Teams and using Microsoft Lists
description:
What is this session about?
Microsoft Lists is a new feature from Microsoft that together with Power Apps in Microsoft Teams make a good comination to modernize the flow and availability of information in organizations. Learn about what Microsoft Lists are and how they can be a good data source for Power Apps in Teams. In the end you will see demo of how this combination can be beneficial to you.

Who is it aimed at?
This session is aimed at managers and business decision makers and you who influence in making decisions on digitalization. Citizen developers are a good fit as well.

Why should I attend?
You will get a taste of how to create powerful solutions to modernize the flow and availability in your organizations digital journey.

title: How Data and AI are Shaping Innovation in Industry
description:
Paul Maher, GM of Industry Experiences in Microsoft’s Cloud and AI group, will host a panel with thought-leaders in the cloud partner ecosystem as they discuss the transformative ideas and technologies shaping the industry.

Slides from event here: https://aka.ms/InnovationinIndustry-Slides

Paul Maher, GM of Industry Experiences, Microsoft
Drew Johansson, Global Alliance Manager, Matillion
Lucas Gorganchian, Co-Founder & CEO, Prismaretail.ai
Sunny Neogi, Chief Growth Officer, Kensci

title: .NetConf Virtual Event | Creating Native iOS + Android Apps in C# using Xamarin
description:
Do you love C# and want to create an iOS or Android app? Me too!

Xamarin enables .NET developers to create native Android and iOS apps in C#.

Xamarin gives C# developers access to 100% of the native Android and iOS APIs, allowing .NET developers to create fully native iOS and Android apps. This means that everything you can do in Swift, ObjC, Java or Kotlin, you can do in Xamarin!

Join me as we discuss the secret-sauce that powers Xamarin and then jump into a live-coding demo where we create our first Xamarin app.

Slides can be found here: Creating Native iOS & Android Apps in C# (codetraveler.io)

Speaker:
Brandon Minnick, Cloud Advocate, Microsoft

I am on the Developer Advocate team at Microsoft, and I love C#, .NET, and Mobile App development. I worked at Xamarin (before the Microsoft acquisition) and continue to share my passions with fellow Xamarin, C# and Cloud developers. I am an avid coder and have developed countless apps. I love working closely with the developer community, helping fellow mobile app and cloud developers make 5-star apps.

title: FusionDev Story
description:
This session is about Luise (maker) and Elio (developer), who joint forces and founded an online sticker shop called pimpyourowndevice.com based on Microsoft services like M365, Power Platform, Azure Functions and Github. 

Who is it aimed at? 
Makers, who want to understand, why the FusionDev approach is beneficial for the outcome of your projects, developers, who can learn that Power platform is also made for them, Business decision makers who will figure out, that there is more than just Collaboration in Teams, that needs to be leveraged. Why should you attend? Hear about an engaging story, learn about the indie approach to create a real-world business and how #betterTogether comes to life. 

Speaker: 
Luise Freese - https://twitter.com/LuiseFreese 
Luise is a Microsoft 365 Consultant based in Germany, MVP for Office Apps & Services, kick-butt Power Apps Developer, SketchNote Artist, blogger, speaker and stickerpreneur at pimpyourowndevice.com. She loves all things Lego, Community, Microsoft 365, calls herself a 'professional learner and too lazy runner" and strongly believes in the Sharing Is Caring mission. You can find her 24/7 on twitter. 

Elio Struyf Elio is an independent Engineering Lead working for Valo Intranet, Blogger, and Speaker on a mission to share his tried-and-true wisdom with as many IT developers as possible. Armed with a deep-rooted passion for all things information technology, he has always been of the belief that one’s job should go beyond something that just “pays the bills”. What you do for a living should leave you feeling inspired every day of your life. For the last 10 years, he has been immersed in Office 365 and SharePoint development, earning multiple awards along the way. He has also had the opportunity to share his know-how at various speaking engagements and create articles for his blog that help others on their professional journeys.

title: Power BI Introduction - Christmas Carols
description:
What is this session about?
Lets look at text analysis of Christmas Carols. We'll look at how you can break up text, use some premium features to look at sentiment analysis and pull out phrases and then use some custom visual such as word cloud to visualise the carols.

Who is it aimed at?
Someone starting out with Power BI and wanting to do something different from the standard sales report.

Why should I attend?
Companies are full of text, we send emails, write reports and send tweets. Can Power BI show any information on what we write and the words we use.

Prerequisites
None although some examples will be using premium features which are part of the Premium per user trial which is currently in preview and free till April.

title: .NetConf Virtual Event | Introduction to Identity for Developers
description:
If you ever had to deal with identity within your solutions then this is the session for you. Join JP and Christos to find out how to implement authentication and authorization for your applications using the Microsoft Identity platform. We will show you how to use our libraries with your favorite language to quickly connect to Azure Active Directory and authenticate your users in a few, basic steps. Get ready for demos and examples the highlight how the Microsoft Identity Platform allows you to create scalable and secure applications.

Speakers:
Christos Mastskas, Senior PM, Microsoft
Christos Matskas is a software developer, dad, blogger, husband, speaker, and all around geek. He currently works as a Developer Advocate for Microsoft Identity helping developers and teams leverage the power of the identity and cloud. Before joining Microsoft, he was a successful entrepreneur collaborating with companies such as MarkIT, Lockheed Martin and Barclays. He's been building software for over 15 years and he's a passionate Open Source advocate. He contributes regularly to numerous OSS projects and works closely with the developer community to make the space bigger and better.

JP Dandison, Principal PM, Microsoft
John (or JP, or John Patrick - many wake words, like Alexa) has been building and deploying software for 16 years, focused on cloud since 2010. Before Microsoft, he worked as an enterprise developer, then launched a completely cloud-native start-up, which was awarded patents for cloud-based tech. Since coming to Microsoft, he has worked to help developers focus on building software that matters and transforming their businesses with cloud and modern identity. Currently, he works as a PM in developer advocacy in the Microsoft Identity Division.

title: Microsoft for Startups Lunch Club - WeAct (Hebrew)
description:
WeAct ראיוון עם מייסדת חברת 
מית שורצנברג, מיקרוסופט פור סטארטאפ, עדי שטיין, מנהלת קשרי מפתחים, מיקרוסופט

Every Tuesday meet the most influential people in the startup industry. This week we are proud to host Darya Henig Shaked Founder & CEO of WeAct
WeAct Ventures was founded by Darya Henig Shaked. With a mission to advance women entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley, Darya founded WEAct in 2016, an international community of 2800+ entrepreneurs worldwide. From over 1,000 applicants, Darya has selected and successfully supported 40 female-founded startups, including Realface, which was acquired by Apple in 2017. in 1/2018 she inaugurated the first shared office space for women entrepreneurs in the Bay Area a in Down Town Los Altos.
Darya previously served as COO at Vital Capital Fund, a $350M private equity fund investing in Sub-Saharan Africa. She has extensive experience in public-private collaborations. Earlier in her career. she was recruited by Israel’s then Prime Minister, Ehud Barak, where she served on his communications team and was Chief of Staff at the Prime Minister’s office and, separately, at Israel’s Ministry of Housing & Construction.

title: Azure Fundamentals Track: Core Azure Concepts - Describe Core Azure Architectural Components(Hebrew)
description:
In this module, you'll examine the various concepts, resources, and terminology that are necessary to work with Azure architecture. For example, you'll learn about Azure subscriptions and management groups, resource groups and Azure Resource Manager, as well as Azure regions and availability zones.
Learning objectives:
• Azure subscriptions and management groups.
• Azure resources, resource groups, and Azure Resource Manager.
• Azure regions, region pairs, and availability zones.
We'll be covering this Learn module: https://aka.ms/Azure_Architectural_2

Presenters: Avihai Hajaj- CTO at Cloud Edge and Microsoft MVP (Azure); Eli Shlomo- Global InfoSec & DevSecOps, Microsoft MVP & Community Leader

title: Introduction to Python for Space Exploration
description: In this workshop we explore how Python plays a role in the innovative solutions that NASA creates. Through the lens of space discovery, this workshop could ignite a passion to persistently learn, discover, and create so that you too can one day help us all understand a little more about the world beyond our Earth. We'll start with an introduction to the types of space exploration problems that Python and data science can influence, then install the tools we need for development, and write some basic Python in Visual Studio Code. If you'd like to follow along, we'll be going through this content on Microsoft Learn: https://aka.ms/PythoninSpace-2 .

title: How Attackers Exploit Containerised Azure Workloads
description:
Containers have been around for a long time. But recently, they have become commonplace within the enterprise. The Azure platform continues to extend services that we can use to host containerized applications (ACR, AKS, ACI, App Service, Function App, Batch, e.t.c). In this session, we'll be going over the Azure containerization coverage, container security threat landscape for Azure, major techniques that attackers use to exploit containerized workloads.
Who is it aimed at?
Anyone interested in understanding container security; Anyone interested in understanding how to Pentest containerized workloads in Azure.

title: D&I Programming for Accessibility
description:
Diversity & Inclusion Global Series 
Programming for Accessibility 

The first event in a new monthly event series, which explores different ways the tech industry can adapt to drive inclusivity, diversity and accessibility for all. This fireside chat with Microsoft Cloud Advocate Rory Preddy, takes a deep dive into Programming for Accessibility.

title: Predict Human Activity with Random Forest Classification
description:
In this workshop we will learn about and create a model using random forest classification. With random forest, decision trees are created based on data samples and then predictions are made about which class they belong to. We'll use data collected by smartphone sensors to detect what activity a person is performing, from walking, sitting, standing, or laying down. This workshop is for people who have a basic understanding of Machine Learning Fundamentals. 
To follow along, you'll need Visual Studio Code and Python installed.

title: Enabling Cloud Magic by Using Azure DevOps Pipelines Release Gates
description:
What is this session about?
Software and platform deployments are made much easier and efficient in public cloud. However, the lifecycle management of these is not getting easier. Both developers and system administrators are moving to CI/CD pipelines to help in this challenge. But pipelines are nothing but the engine, performing the hard work. What we miss is the brains, the sparkles that make pipelines running in a magical way… Imagine being able to run a pipeline deployment only by approval from your software lead? Or what’s the point in running an Azure pipeline deployment, if the Azure service is down, the region is unavailable or your Azure governance policies are blocking the deployment? That’s the magic I’m talking about. And that’s exactly what Azure DevOps has built-in using Release Gates. Learn in this session from Peter De Tender, Azure Technical Trainer EMEA at Microsoft, what Release Gates are, how to manage them and seeing them in action. As usual in Peter’s sessions, this will be a demo-packed delivery. 

Who is it aimed at?
Developers, cloud admins, cloud architects and anyone who is new to or experienced in Azure DevOps Pipelines, who wants to learn how to run them in an even more optimized way. 

Why should I attend?
Azure DevOps Pipelines Release Gates are the brain, the decision makers if you want, on when a pipeline should run or not. Automating this process, dramatically optimizes your platform lifecycle management. 

Prerequisites:
Having basic understanding of Azure, CI/CD pipeline concepts is beneficial, though not required.

title: Como implementar sua infra no Azure de modo consistente usando ARM Templates
description:
Não há como ignorar a importância da computação em nuvem e como ela tem transformado a realidade da tecnologia nas empresas e nos serviços que consumimos no dia a dia. Mas quais são as diferenças e vantagens da nuvem? Ela realmente é ágil como ouvimos falar?

Esclareça essas e outras dúvidas durante nossa apresentação sobre ARM Templates no Microsoft Azure, um passo decisivo para se beneficiar da agilidade e flexibilidade que a nuvem trouxe para o mercado de tecnologia, além de entender com a automação da infraestrutura é crucial para que soluções complexas possam atender milhares de usuários ao redor do globo.

 Aprenda mais sobre esse assunto e complete essa trilha de aprendizado #LearnSession para ganhar uma badge: https://aka.ms/AzureARMTemplates-11

 Palestrantes:
- Isabella Pirani
Isabella Pirani é Bacharel em Ciência e Tecnologia e Engenheira de Informação pela Universidade Federal do ABC. Hoje ela é consultora de Azure Cloud & AI na Microsoft, além de ser curiosa por essência, amar os animais e acreditar no poder da educação como ferramenta para transformar o mundo.

- Ramon Sanches
Consultor de Azure Cloud na Microsoft, atuando há 20 anos em TI conduziu projetos complexos em empresas dos mais diversos setores. Soma ainda experiências em Data Center, Outsourcing, Suporte e Gestão de Operações, agregando uma visão aprofundada dos desafios da tecnologia. Entusiasta das causas sociais, é formado em Gestão de Negócios Sociais pela ESPM e trabalha com ações de transformação pedagógica no ensino público.

title: Getting the most out of your IoT data: basics of Predictive Maintenance
description: Organizations are routinely faced with the challenge of how to analyze their IoT data. This talk will focus on companies who collect data from their factory operations and are interested in predicting mechanical failures. The audience will get an overview of the entire process starting with how to formulate their business problem, perform feature engineering and build a predictive maintenance model using Python using both traditional/Deep learning techniques.

title: Microsoft Tech Days: A Developer’s Guide to AI
description:
Each of our Tech Days events incorporates a series of sessions on a technical topic, interspersed with guests from the technical community, as well as stories from Microsoft customers & partners. 

In our first edition, host Amy Boyd will bring you A Developer's Guide to AI. Perhaps you've heard about Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals - a technical certification for engineers, data scientists and developers? This Tech Day is a great way of getting started in your AI journey and working towards certification. It's also a great way of introducing yourself to some of the AI & Machine Learning features available in Azure, from a developer perspective

Presenter:
Amy Boyd, Senior Cloud Advocate, Microsoft

title: Introduction to Power BI | Tea & Biscuits
description:
What is this session about?
Using different data sources to create a Power BI displaying a map of tea production and favourite biscuit types in the UK. We will start with a blank report, fetch and transform the data ready to display in visuals on the report and then publish to Power BI service.
Who is it aimed at?
Beginners in Power BI
Why should I attend?
New report writers who want to learn hints and tips
Speaker Info:
Laura Graham-Brown, MVP
Over 20 year experience at being passionate about training, solving problems and loving a new challenge. I have worked with household names and clients very few will know, from the huge corporate to the small business, helping them make SharePoint, Flow, PowerApps, Power BI and Office solve their business needs.
Pre-requisites:
It is assumed you have Power BI desktop installed.

title: Create your Own Blockchain Network
description:
What is this session about?
This is the second session in a three-part series on blockchain technology. In this session, we'll create our own blockchains using Visual Studio Code and the Blockchain Development Kit extension. We'll write, test, and deploy our contracts to a local blockchain network running on the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

Who is it aimed at?
This is designed for those who have a basic understanding of blockchain technology and want to get some hands-on experience.

Why should you join?
We will explore blockchain development together and discover tools and strategies that can be used to program applications.

About the speaker
Meaghan Lewis has been working in the tech industry for over a decade. She is currently a Technical Program Manager at Microsoft and focuses on creating and delivering learning experiences centered around emerging technologies such blockchain and quantum computing. Meaghan enjoys tinkering on personal projects and collaborating with other enthusiasts to explore new things. She is a California native who currently lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with her husband and two dogs.

You will need to have Visual Studio Code installed, and a basic understanding of blockchain technology to follow along.

https://aka.ms/blockchain-development-11

title: Implement DataOps by using Azure Data Factory and Azure DevOps
description:
One task that tends to elude data professionals is how to integrate data operations into a DevOps pipeline. In this session, we will discuss DataOps and how to incorporate your data engineering tasks into an Azure DevOps pipeline. This session will include an overview presentation as well as in-depth demonstrations. Attendees will learn the building blocks necessary to incorporate DataOps into their standard development practices.

Find the Speakers slides here: https://aka.ms/ImplementingDataOps

Speaker: Ted Malone, Data and AI Cloud Solution Architect, Microsoft’s West Region
In this current role, Ted engages with Microsoft’s customers to evangelize and support the Microsoft Data and AI story and to educate them on new and exciting ways to gain insight from both unstructured and structured data within their environments as well as incorporate Microsoft’s suite of Advanced Analytics and Machine Learning capabilities.
Prior to joining Microsoft, Ted was a Software Architect in the CTO office for EMC, where he led the design and development of enterprise storage management solutions that leverage Big Data and complex Business Intelligence technologies.
Ted is a “Data Guy” that has developed and deployed data insight solutions for more than two decades, and has worked with Microsoft SQL Server since version 1 (Which was installed on OS/2).
Ted has been a featured speaker at many industry conferences and events, including Microsoft’s Federal Forum, Microsoft Tech Ed, Microsoft TechReady, Meritalk, AFCEA, The Professional Association for SQL Server (PASS), Dev Connections and many more.

title: Machine Learning in C#?! Introduction to ML.NET
description:
If you're a .NET developer, you may be forgiven for thinking that in order to build awesome machine learning applications, you'll need to brush up on your Python skills in order to use ML libraries, or even worse, buy food for that data scientist in your team until they've built an ML model for you.

With the release of ML.NET, this is no longer the case!

In this session, I'll cover what ML.NET is and how you can use it to add machine learning capabilities to your .NET applications. I'll cover the capabilities that the API offers in terms of preparing our data and evaluating our models. I'll also talk about the capabilities that the ML.NET Model builder and how that can simplify how we choose what type of model we want to build and I'll also talk about how we can deploy our models into production.

So ditch that data scientist (in a nice way of course) and come and see how you can leverage your existing .NET skills to use ML.NET to build some interesting machine learning applications!

About your speaker:
Will Velida
I'm a Software Engineer based in Auckland, New Zealand and a Data Platform MVP. I spend my time attempting to build cool things in .NET and Azure. I have a particular focus on Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Functions. I also like to play around with ML.NET and Spark on .NET.

I have spoken at conferences in a variety of different countries across the world, speaking on topics such as Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Functions and Azure Databricks.

I also blog regularly on platforms such as Medium and DEV.to.

title: Dando os primeiros passos com C# (Portuguese)
description:
A linguagem de programação C # oferece grande produtividade, versatilidade e é a linguagem de programação mais poderosa para o .NET Framework. Se você tem interesse em se tornar uma pessoa programadora C#, este workshop é um grande primeiro passo.

Você vai começar a aprender o básico da sintaxe escrevendo seu primeiro código C #. Em seguida, você explorará como armazenar e recuperar dados em aplicativos e como realizar a formatação básica de dados.

Você sairá deste workshop com um maior conhecimento sobre programação em C # e recursos para ajudá-lo a continuar sua jornada.

 Pré-requisitos
Experiência anterior em programação é útil, mas não obrigatória.

title: Getting Started with Azure Command and Query
description:
So, you want to migrate to Azure? You’ve read the success stories, and you see the benefits yourself. But just how do you get started? And how do you convince those who don’t see the benefits as you do? In this talk, we will get started on the Azure development route. Using a site that communicates with a Web API and then, using message queues and functions, to store data from the user in table storage. And creating the resources needed to deploy the app within the Azure portal! So that when you leave you can explore for yourself! 
Who should attend? Software developers interested in getting started with Azure. 
Why attend? Because you want to get started it Azure, but are not sure where to get started, this session will give you that insight Prerequisites for this session: Working understanding of C#, interest in Azure.

title: Supercharge Your .Net Apps!
description:
Did you know that all this is easily achieved with Azure Spring Cloud architecture?
Join Rory from the Azure Team as they show you recent Azure Spring Cloud Steeltoe advancements and how easy it is to integrate these to design scalable, secure, and highly available .NET Cloud solutions. We’ll be live-coding real-world applications that demonstrate:
-Migrating an existing .NET app to Azure Spring Cloud with no code changes
-Exciting new Roadmap backed by both VMWare and Microsoft.

title: Secure Access to Azure VMs with Azure Bastion
description: Azure Bastion is a new way to easily and securely access Azure VMs over RDP or SSH. Forget jump hosts and stop using public IPs to reach Azure VMs in an insecure manner. With Azure Bastion, you have a new feature to securely access Azure VMs from around the world. This session gives you a full view on Azure Bastion. Learn how it works, all about the requirements and how to harden the service. See how easy it is to register the service, replace existing jumg hosts to improve the security of your network and learn all about upcoming features.

description:

description:
Pulumi is an open source infrastructure as code SDK that enables you to create, deploy, and manage infrastructure on any cloud. title: C# 7, 8, and 9 Can Completely Change the Way you Write Code
description:
Many .NET developers come from a long, rich history of development and it can be tempting to ignore the new “functional-ish” language features coming to C#. Fear not, these new language features can completely reinvent the way you build C# applications.
In this quick session, we will look at new language features in the last 3 major releases of C# and how they can completely transform the way we write our everyday code. Join us for a fun, interactive session where we will build a sample application using many of these features in real-time.

Sample code can be found here:

Sidney Andrews is a native of Richmond, VA, an Azure MVP, and a Microsoft Certified Trainer. Sidney has authored multiple developer and Azure courses on http://edx.org. Sidney has been featured as a presenter on Channel 9, Ignite and Build. Sidney specializes in finding ways to open-source training on Azure and .NET topics.

title: DevOps Tools of the Trade
description: From cloning a GitHub repo to setting up an Azure Pipeline, DevOps tools are a critical aspect to developing scalable, professional software. By using the proper services, you can plan smarter, collaborate better, and ship faster. In this workshop, get an introduction to an array of key DevOps tools and documentation resources that will prepare you for your next large project.

title: PowerShell Fundamentals
description:
PowerShell is a cross-platform task automation and configuration management framework. In this session recording, we cover how to utilize PowerShell to manage Office 365 and on-premise environments with Active Directory and Microsoft Exchange with multiple objects. We also discuss how to utilize automation runbooks or Scheduled tasks to simplify automation.

title: Solving problems! And What We Could Learn from COVID19
description:
Since March 2020, companies have had to change the way they approach problems. What if the COVID19 crisis was an opportunity for us to return to a more pragmatic management of our problems? What if the survival of our businesses depended on our ability to question the approach to the needs of our customers or our users of the IT resources we provide them? Frugal... Jugaad... how can we keep the pragmatism and efficiency of March 2020?

Join this talk with Microsoft MVP, Nicolas Georgault, to learn how cloud and the Microsoft ecosystem can help you to solve problems simply and get things done to keep your business close to your users and customers needs.

title: Modern Workplace Security with M365 - Zero Trust Architecture
description:
Today, in the modern era of Cloud, there exists an abundance of security solutions and yet what will actually make you secure remains obscure. Join us for this session to get your much needed answers on the steps you can quickly take leveraging Microsoft 365 suite to protect yourself against the most prevalent current and emerging threats while leveraging zero trust model. We will discuss top things you can and should do to secure your modern workplace. We will be covering everything from securely accessing your environment, to making sure you can respond appropriately when and if needed.

We will discuss:
- Intelligent Security
- Threat actors exposure to breach
- How to create a plan/strategy
- integrated end to end solutions
- Secure authentication - Zero Trust
- Threat protection
- Device and Information security
- How to Monitor, Detect, and Respond
- Action Items

Speaker: Riaz Javed Butt, Lead Architect; Microsoft Azure, Office Apps & Services MVP

title: Rust Programming Basics
description: Rust is a programming language that empowers developers to build reliable and efficient software. It is fun to write, easy to read, and high performing. In this workshop, we will explore how to start coding in Rust. This workshop will require you to use VS Code and the Rust extension to write code.

description:

title: Azure Analytics Options
description:
From big data to millions of tiny IoT devices, data is useless if you cannot analyze it. Azure Analytics offers a wide array of tools that can operate many times faster than-and cost a fraction of-other cloud offerings. In this stream, we’ll introduce the analytic services available on Azure.

She has dedicated her life to finding effective ways to teach and learn various computer science topics, particularly focusing on creating learning experiences that enculturate learners and provide a holistic learning experience, rather than a tutorial-like experience. title: “Go” Further with the Go Programming Language
description:
Go quickly became a hot language for low-level systems development, databases, and distributed systems, but the language has expanded well beyond systems development. Have you heard of Docker, Kubernetes, and CockroachDB? They’re all written in Go. You can even build full web apps with Go. In this session, we’ll briefly learn the history of Go and then dive into the language and its libraries for writing web services. Finally, we’ll build a REST API using Go, deploy it to the web, and test it.

Presenter: Aaron Schlesinger

Aaron Schlesinger is a Microsoft Senior Cloud Developer Advocate focusing on Go, containers, and Kubernetes on the Azure platform. He does extensive work in the Go and Kubernetes communities, including holding leadership positions on major Go and Kubernetes open source projects. He is currently a core maintainer of the Athens project (https://github.com/gomods/athens) and created and runs the Go in 5 Minutes screencast series (https://goin5minutes.com/).

description:
The world of Azure is vast, and the ways in which developers can integrate services and tools are even greater. In this session, we’ll explore various options as Sarah Guthals discovers, creates-and likely fails at-Azure APIs.

title: Intro to Python Programming
description: Python is an interpreted, high-level, general-purpose programming language and one of the best for data science and machine learning. This workshop explores the basics of Python, such as arithmetic, numeric, and data types. By the end, you’ll gain the familiarity you need to start using it on your own. In this workshop, we will use Python examples within a Jupyter Notebook in VS Code.

title: Drinking from the IoT Data Firehose
description:
IoT generates data-A LOT of data. To add to the complexity, this data can be streamed from a variety of devices and run the scope from a home with a single sensor to a factory with millions of them. So…where does all this data go once it is sent? In this session, we'll take that next step to look at how you can take the glut of IoT data and make it useful. We’ll query the data it in real time, analyzing it with code and storing it in a database, such as a CosmosDB, for future offline analysis.

Presenter: Jim Bennett

Jim Bennett does things with IoT and Azure in the Developer Relations team at Microsoft, mainly creating content for students and faculty to help them be successful with Microsoft technologies. He’s British, so sounds way smarter than he actually is, and is happy he moved to Redmond in time to be locked down at home and not see the office he came to work in, or the places he wanted to visit. He has lived in four continents as a developer in the mobile, desktop, and scientific spaces. He also hates cats, but has a 7-year-old daughter who loves cats…so he has two cats.

description:
GitHub is no longer just a place to store your code. That’s a good thing, because the work doesn't end after code has been pushed or merged. There are unit tests to execute, linting to run, and deployments to push. With GitHub Actions, you can perform any of these activities based on the events you define. Join us in this session for a conversation on GitHub Actions and take your repositories to the next level!

description:
Power Platform tools such as Power Apps, Power Virtual Agent and Power Automate allow to integrate AI smart solutions in an quick and easy process for business to achieve smarter solutions. In this hour today, we will go through some solutions and steps to implement AI solutions using Power Apps and Power Virtual agents. In this session, we will follow through some examples and steps to implement them.

title: Add AI to Your Applications the Easy Way
description:
Did you know you can add artificial intelligence (AI) to an application without creating your own models, GPUs, or terabytes of training data? In fact, AI can be distilled to a couple of API or REST calls if you are using the right services, like Azure Cognitive Services. Azure Cognitive Services is a suite of AI services and cognitive APIs you can call from within new or existing applications. With Cognitive Services, you can do cool things like detect text in pictures, translate text, and even provide sentiment analysis. In this workshop, you’ll learn more about Cognitive Services and how to add pre-built models to an application.

Prerequisites:
This workshop assumes you have had previous experience using Python.

Presenter: Bhavuk Chawla 
Bhavuk Chawla has over 15 years of hands-on, professional experience in IT and more than six years of experience in Big Data and Machine Learning. Bhavuk has a B.E. in Computer Engineering from the Netaji Subhas University of Technology (NSIT) and an M.S. in Software Systems from the Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS).

Bhavuk spends his time on Big Data analytics projects involving Hadoop, Spark, NoSQL, Google Cloud, Azure and the AWS stack. He has implemented end-to-end data science projects, from content acquisition to production deployment, and has implemented various machine learning algorithms using Mahout and Spark ML.

As a technical architect, Bhavuk has contributed to the strategic direction of multiple projects, and has supported all aspects of the project lifecycle, including planning, installation, configuration, maintenance and monitoring. As an instructor, Bhavuk excels at providing technical mentorship to students, sharing his first-hand knowledge and helping to guide their Big Data journeys.

You can learn more about Bhavuk at https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhavuk-chawla/.

In fact, AI can be distilled to a couple of API or REST calls if you are using the right services, like Azure Cognitive Services. Azure Cognitive Services is a suite of AI services and cognitive APIs you can call from within new or existing applications. With Cognitive Services, you can do cool things like detect text in pictures, translate text, and even provide sentiment analysis. In this workshop, you’ll learn more about Cognitive Services and how to add pre-built models to an application.

Prerequisites:
This workshop assumes you have had previous experience using Python.

Speaker Bio:
Maddie Shang,
AI Researcher / Research Engineer
Maddie has 6+ years of experience in tech as a venture capitalist (CFA L3), was a 2x startup founder, Sr. Data Scientist and then AI / Blockchain Researcher. Her work in AI with OpenMined is currently funded by Pytorch (Facebook). She works as an AI Researcher / Engineer in industry, is the Founder and Global Lead of Data Science at Women Who Code (with 1k+ global data professional members) and advisor to various startups. She completed her degree in Mathematics at the University of Waterloo and is currently based out of Cambridge MA. Maddie enjoys piloting airplanes and adventures in the wilderness in her spare time.

title: Power BI Introduction - Reporting on Tasks
description:
This session will start from the very basics of Power BI using a task list as a data set. It will cover connecting to your data, performing some transformations to tidy up the data, modelling the data to add relationships and calculations, building a calendar and then using visuals to report on task progress, and finally look to publish the report to the Power BI service. The final report will include multiple pages, charts, slicers and data cards to help a manager report on their projects.
A copy of the data will be available and a copy of the final report will be made available.

title: How Automated Machine Learning Reduces Time to Insights
description:
Determining meaningful answers from large, complex datasets is a difficult and lengthy problem, even with the support of validated machine learning algorithms. In this session, you will learn about the functionality of Azure’s automated machine learning (ML) service. The Azure Auto ML service not only helps you build ML models efficiently using one algorithm, but then compares dozens of algorithm setups, scores them, and helps you gain insights from multiple perspectives. Ultimately, it allows data scientists, analysts, and developers to build ML models with high-scale efficiency and productivity, all while sustaining model quality.

Presenter: Amy Boyd
Amy Boyd is a Cloud Advocate at Microsoft, specializing in data science and machine learning. Her role as a Cloud Advocate is to help developers to learn, engage, and build on the Microsoft AI platform. Amy creates and delivers online and in-person content and works with developers to provide the best product experience.

Additional Resources:
Responsible ML: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/machine-learning/responsibleml/
Session Resources on GitHub: https://github.com/microsoft/Reactors/tree/main/online-event-resources/data-science-and-machine-learning/automated-machine-learning
What is AutoML: aka.ms/mythbuster-automl
Understand Automated Machine Learning Results: aka.ms/automl-metrics

title: Use modelos de aprendizado de máquina para dominar seus dados
description:
Novos dados são criados diariamente, e mais dados geralmente significa mais problemas. Neste workshop, saiba como ensinar as máquinas a analisar cenários complexos em grande escala. Primeiramente, vamos limpar e organizar os dados e depois vamos treinar e testar modelos de aprendizado de máquina. Terminaremos com a publicação de suas previsões online para compartilhar com outras pessoas.

 Palestrante:
- Pedro O. S. Vaz de Melo
Pedro O.S. Vaz de Melo é professor adjunto do Departamento de Ciência da Computação (DCC) da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG). É formado (2003) e mestre (2007) em Ciência da Computação pela Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Minas Gerais (2003). Ele obteve seu doutorado na Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG), com período de um ano como pesquisador visitante na Universidade Carnegie Mellon e de cinco meses como pesquisador visitante no INRIA Lyon. Seu interesse de pesquisa é principalmente focado na descoberta de conhecimento e mineração de dados em sistemas complexos e distribuídos. Pedro publicou mais de sessenta artigos revisados por pares em periódicos, revistas e conferências como ACM SIGKDD, Neurips, WWW, ICWSM, ACM TKDD, PLOS ONE e IEEE Commag. Ele também foi coordenador de diversos projetos financiados pelo CNPq e Fapemig e recebeu dois Google Research Awards para a América Latina.

Saiba mais sobre este evento no Meetup do Reactor São Paulo: https://www.meetup.com/pt-BR/Microsoft-Reactor-Sao-Paulo/events/271212479/

title: AI on the Microsoft Stack
description: In this session we do a deep dive into the A.I. stack that Microsoft has to offer. We start with pre-trained Cognitive services like Computer Vision, Anomaly Detection and Speaker recognition. And move on to the more advanced tooling like Machine Learning Studio and Azure Machine Learning Services.

title: Azure Blockchain Beyond the Hype
description: Learn more about what is Blockchain, Real Microsoft Case Studies and How to use Azure Blockhain Workbench to accelerate your Blockchain PoC journey.

title: How to Accelerate the End-to-End Machine Learning Lifecycle on Azure
description:
This Azure ML session is for all who want to know how to:
- create code-free ML models (using AutoML as well as the drag & drop pipeline creation method)
- create ML models using Python (created either in Azure Notebooks or locally)
- directly use pre-built ML models under Azure Cognitive APIs
We will also cover the end-to-end ML life cycle; how to train ML models, how ML models can be versioned and deployed for inference, and we can use them as part of other DevOps, data warehousing or ETL pipelines.

title: Go-to-Market Strategies for Turbulent Times
description:
Join this session to learn some key tips & tricks to align your go-to-market strategy to the current landscape - how to match sales capacity to changing market opportunities, shifting to lower cost coverage where possible, re-prioritizing your digital roadmap, and much more. You’ll also get a chance to raise your own questions and have them addressed live by our speaker, Shaloo Garg, Managing Director of Silicon Valley and the Southwest, Microsoft for Startups and special guests Swapnil Jain, CEO & Founder Observe.ai, and Sean Knapp, CEO & Founder, Ascend.io

Speakers:

Shaloo Garg is currently Managing Director of Silicon Valley and the Southwest region for Microsoft for Startups. She brings a combination of strong startup, enterprise, strategic partnership and corporate development experience. Previously, Shaloo was at Oracle at Global Oracle Innovation where she led Global Corporate Innovation practice of commercializing revenue opportunities for startups into the enterprise client base and partner ecosystem. She has also lead go-to-market for Oracle’s cloud business and was part of the M&A team that acquired Peoplesoft, Siebel, Retek etc. Prior to joining Oracle, she was in a couple of early stage startups. Shaloo is passionate about education and is a “Champion of Innovation” at UN Women where she is spinning up virtual Innovation Labs with Universities leveraging emerging technologies to encourage digital literacy in developing countries for young girls who do not have access to education.

Swapnil Jain is co-founder and CEO of Observe.AI, an agent enablement platform powered by Voice AI that analyzes 100% of customer engagement calls for compliance and coaching. Swapnil comes with a strong background in technology and product at Twitter and Google, and is currently based in San Francisco, CA.

Sean Knapp is the founder and CEO of Ascend.io. Prior to Ascend.io, Sean was a co-founder, CTO, and Chief Product Officer at Ooyala. At Ooyala Sean oversaw Product, Engineering and Solutions, and played key roles in scaling the company to 500+ employees, Ooyala's $410m acquisition, as well as Ooyala's subsequent acquisitions of Videoplaza and Nativ. Sean also developed and launched iGoogle, the company's popular, customizable home page. Sean holds a B.S. and M.S. in Computer Science from Stanford University, and competed for Stanford as a member of the varsity Cross Country and Track & Field teams

description:

description:

title: Using IoT Hub with Xamarin
description:
Come take a deeper dive into the Azure IoT Hub and how to connect it to an application built in Xamarin. In this session, we will build a location tracking app in Xamarin that polls (sends) data to Azure IoT Hub. You’ll learn how to use data from a mobile client app written in Xamarin and how to use it with IoT Hub.
This session uses Xamarin, Visual Studio, Azure IoT Hub, and C# (all free on Azure and Community versions of Visual Studio). This session recommends advanced IoT and Xamarin knowledge.

Speakers: Sweeky Satpathy, Ben Buttigieg

Sweekriti Satpathy is a Senior Software Engineer with the Mobile Customer Advisory Team at Microsoft. She is on a mission to preach best practices in mobile app development to the world. Her passions include programming, Legos, music, and food. 

Ben Buttigieg is a Senior Software Engineer on the Mobile Customer Advisory Team (MobCAT), helping enterprise customers get the most out of Xamarin and mobile technologies. title: Build AI bots for Next Wave of Computing with Bot Framework Composer
description:
According to Gartner, conversational AI agents are named as top 3rd digital trend for 2020. Another research shows that bots are going to take over 25% of the retail operations across the world. Do you want to build the similar experience for this new user interface paradigm? If yes, then you’re at the right place! In this session, you will learn about the Microsoft Bot Framework and its latest offerings such as drag and drop, low-code developer tool aka Bot Framework Composer and how can you utilize this visual authoring canvas to build next gen bots. As we build a Flight Tracker demo on the fly, you will also get a chance to learn about essential design principles, handling interruptions in your conversations and integrating it with the Azure Functions / API (all without writing a single line of code) Lastly, you will also see how easy it is to deployed the bots to Microsoft Teams, Facebook Messenger and other channels. All in all, it’s going to be fun for those developers who are interested in developing bots and publishing it to the world.

Presenter: Arafat Tehsin (Microsoft MVP AI)

About your speaker:
Arafat is a Technical Consultant at Velrada and Microsoft MVP (AI). He has been working with Global ISVs of Microsoft and developing some next-gen solutions using cutting-edge Microsoft technologies.

He's also an active contributor for the community especially on the Bot Framework side. He's one of the founding members of Bot Builder Community Project and have been writing / speaking about Bot Framework, Azure Cognitive Services and Power Platform.

title: Power BI | Sales Report
description: Start from the basics and walk through creating a report from a table of data to publishing a two page report to the Power BI service. In this session we will connect to data from 2 sources, add relationships, build a calendar and create measures which will all be used to create a professional report. This session will be based on a simple sales data set which can be supplied ahead of the session so people can duplicate what is being done.

title: MLOps Using Azure Machine Learning
description:
Operationalising ML model release using Azure DevOps

For the longest time data science was often performed in silos, using large scale compute operating across isolated copies of production data. This process was not repeatable, explainable or scalable and often introduced business and security risk. With modern enterprises now adopting a DevOps engineering culture, no longer can machine learning development practice operate in isolation of the business or existing applications teams. This demo heavy session introduces the new Azure ML Services capabilities and how this can assist to bring the practice of data science into the age of modern DevOps.

Presenter: Ananth Prakash - Lead Architect - Data, AI & IoT @ Microsoft

About your speaker:
Ananth Prakash - Lead Architect - Data, AI & IoT @ Microsoft

Ananth has a successful track record in delivery of strategic projects, products and platforms in the Data & AI domain for 16+ years across North America, Australia and Asia. Some of his roles include leading product engineering groups at Oracle, Managing Consultant at IBM and Senior Technical Architect - Data & AI at Infosys. As a Lead Architect at Microsoft, Ananth helps enterprise customers architect & deploy strategic solutions on Azure to accelerate their business transformation journey.

title: How Azure SQL Can Be Your Preferred Database Platform
description:
Join the Azure SQL Product Team to learn how Azure SQL can be your preferred database platform whether you are building modern cloud native applications or migrating legacy applications from those hosted on-premises. In this session, we will walk you through the various options to deploy Azure SQL based on your workload and dive into the features that makes it an effective platform for best return of your investments. We will also discuss the recent innovations and how we are thinking about the future for Azure SQL along with mechanisms / tools to seamlessly migrate your on-premises SQL workloads to Azure SQL.

Presenters: Ajay Jagannathan, Principal Group Program Manager for Azure SQL Data Base and SQL Server Engine PM Team @ Microsoft and Mohamed Kabiruddin, Senior Program Manager Azure SQL PM Team @ Microsoft 

About your speakers:

Ajay Jagannathan is a Principal Group Program Manager for Azure SQL Database and SQL Server Engine PM team, based in Redmond, USA. He has an MS in Computer Science and over 22 years of industry experience. He is currently responsible for driving product strategy and roadmap for the database engine for SQL Server and Azure SQL Database to deliver breakthrough innovations and product experiences from inception to engaged customer usage that modernize database to handle the speed, variety and scale of today's data. He partners closely with several customers to understand product usage and feedback to drive improvements in the product. He has deep experience in various features of SQL database engine spanning over ten versions (SQL 6.5- SQL 2017) and Azure SQL Database.

Mohamed Kabiruddin is a Senior Program Manager in the Azure SQL PM Team and is currently located Sydney, Australia. Prior to joining the Product Team, he was a Cloud Solution Architect working with enterprise customers in Australia and have helped them with SQL migrations and modern data platform implementations in Azure. He has over a decade of experience working with customers and delivering a wide range of projects on SQL Server and Business Intelligence. He is also very passionate about the Data community and love evangelising SQL in community events.

title: Building Apps Super Fast Using the Microsoft Graph Toolkit
description:
The Microsoft Graph Toolkit is allowing Graph powered apps to be created incredibly quickly. Leave this session knowing what the Microsoft Graph is and how to write your first Graph powered web app using the Microsoft Graph Toolkit. description:

title: VIRTUAL WORKSHOP: Docker From Scratch
description:
Docker's popularity has exploded over the last couple of years, especially in the DevOps space, but unless you've spent a lot of time in that area it can be a confusing technology to wrap your head around. So let's step back and start looking at Docker from, well, FROM scratch (and we'll understand just what that means). With minimal starting knowledge of Docker we'll look into what it is, cover off all the core concepts from images to containers, volumes to networks, and how we can compose environments. We'll also look at how to use Docker in Dev, not just DevOps and how containers can be useful tools without being something to run production infrastructure on.

Meet your Speaker: Aaron Powell

Aaron is a Developer Advocate at Microsoft and former consultant at Readify. By day he spends his time in all facets of .NET development and by night he explores crazy ideas like writing your own implementation of numbers in .NET, creating IoC in JavaScript or implementing tic-tac-toe using git commits.

title: Joining and Cleaning datasets with Python and Pandas
description: Datasets usually need a lot of cleaning up and manipulating before they can be analyzed. title: Azure Incident Retrospective: Datacenter cooling, Australia East, Aug 2023 (Tracking ID: VVTQ-J98)
description:

title: 圆桌讨论：与 MVP 对话 - MVP 的 30 周年 | Global Azure 2023 China 广州站
description:
圆桌讨论：与 MVP 对话 - MVP 的 30 周年 | Global Azure 2023 China 广州站

一年一度的 Global Azure 即将到来！

title: 【比特熊充电栈】AOAI 4-用ChatGPT聊天？Azure Open AI不止于此
description:
活动主题：【比特熊充电栈】AOAI 4-用ChatGPT聊天？Azure Open AI不止于此

企业数字化转型是一个长久不衰的话题，因为我们总有新的技术帮助企业提高数字化建设水平。在Open AI之前在企业数字化的有些场景中，我们需要花费极大的成本都不一定满足企业要求，这样的高成本低产出极大的阻碍了人工智能在企业的落地，甚至很多人工智能被嘲笑为人工智障。现在在LLM扶植下，Azure Open AI可以帮助我们高质量地解决之前很多难题，特别是在知识模型，语言理解，和文本构建上，可以帮助企业迅速提高数字化建设水平。本期充电栈我们将从知识萃取，数据治理和智能辅助这三个企业场景的场景为大家带来新的AI赋能体验。

发起这一波AI 2.0浪潮的微软现任CEO纳德拉，曾写过一本《刷新》，提到科技的进步不仅是源于本身的先进，也需要看其被使用的普遍性。Azure OpenAI正是这样一种技术变革，先进且同时易于在各方面采用。哪怕我们还不是很理解多模态大模型的强大，但认知服务已经可以帮助我们随时开启变革-从数字化转型，迈向业务转型。

​

胡浩、王豫翔

description:
IoT · Pi Day 特辑｜Microsoft Azure x NVIDIA 智能语音专场

Pi Day is coming again!

每年的3月14日 Pi Day，都是专属于全球边缘设备开发者们的智能边缘开发盛会，今年当然也不例外。恰逢 Pi Day，由 Microsoft Azure 联合 NVIDIA 企业开发者社区，共同推出的“Microsoft Azure & NVIDIA IoT 开发者季”系列活动也迎来了第三季--智能语音专题。

本期，微软高级云技术布道师卢建晖，将同 NVIDIA 企业级开发者社区高级经理李奕澎一起，结合 Microsoft Azure、自然语言与智能边缘技术，为大家带来智能语音专场，实践“云+边缘”的 IoT 解决方案。

分享嘉宾：
李奕澎
NVIDIA 企业级开发者社区经理
拥有多年数据分析与人工智能自然语言处理开发经验。
在自动语音识别，自然语言处理，自然语言理解方面有着丰富的实战经验与见解。曾主导完成基于 NLP 的智能对话，智能信息抽取，意图识别，文本分类等多个项目。

分享主题：使用 NVIDIA NeMo 训练 TTS 语音合成模型
语音合成又称文语转换技术（Text to speech，TTS），能将任意文字信息转化为标准流畅的自然的语音朗读出来，相当于给机器装上了人工嘴巴，将文字用声音给它说出来，实现一种语言播报的效果，该技术被广泛的应用在对话式 AI 相关如智能音箱产品当中。本小节将重点介绍如何使用 NVIDIA NeMo 训练 TTS 语音合成模型。

卢建晖
微软高级云技术布道师 
微软高级云技术布道师，热爱编程，热爱分享，专注在人工智能，物联网，云原生等领域。

分享主题：结合 OpenAI 用 Jetson NX 搭建智能音箱
智能音箱是非常受欢迎的边缘设备，可以为生活和工作提供各种便利。本次课程会结合 OpenAI ，Azure Speech 以及 Jetson NX 完成相关的简易智能音箱搭建。

title: Explainable AI (XAI) Course: Local Explanations - Concept and Methods
description:
The XAI course provides a comprehensive overview of explainable AI, covering both theory and practice, and exploring various use cases for explainability. Participants will learn not only how to generate explanations, but also how to evaluate and effectively communicate these explanations to diverse stakeholders.

The XAI course is managed on a voluntary basis by DataNights and Microsoft organizers and free for charge for the participant. This course is designed for data scientists that have at least two years in industry of hands-on experience with machine learning and Python and a basic background in deep learning. Some of the sessions will be held in-person at the Microsoft Reactor in Tel Aviv, while others will be conducted virtually.

Course Leaders: 
Bitya Neuhof, DataNights 
Yasmin Bokobza, Microsoft 

What is this session about? 
Machine learning models can be analyzed at a high level using global explanations, such as linear model coefficients. However, there are several limitations to these global explanations. In this talk, I will review the use cases where local explanations are needed and introduce two popular methods for generating local explanations: LIME and SHAP. Our learning will be focused on SHAP, its theory, model-agnostic and model-specific versions, and how to use and read SHAP visualizations.

如今，作为一名微软 MVP，他仍然在技术分享与快乐编程的道路上继续走着；而与此同时，作为一名“大龄”程序员，他也同样有着自己的人生选择和挑战。

作为一款现代化的浏览器，Edge 支持扩展功能。这允许开发人员添加或修改 Edge 功能，改善浏览器的用户体验。如果你有基于特定 Web 浏览器或特定网页功能改进的想法或产品，可以创建 Edge 扩展，进而发布上架并付诸使用。 

本次分享，我们就来聊聊 Edge 浏览器的扩展。两位来自 Microsoft Edge 团队，同时有着丰富浏览器插件开发经验的软件工程师，将在线为我们讲解 Edge 浏览器的扩展，介绍 Edge 扩展的发布、上架与运营，并结合 Demo 为我们进行在线演示。

title: 学生大使技能秀 ｜.NET 入门
description:
学生大使技能秀 ｜.NET 入门
“微软学生大使”（Microsoft Learn Student Ambassador，简称 MLSA）是微软针对全球范围内的在校学生所设立的项目，旨在鼓励那些在校园里积极倡导、推动创新实践，乐于积极帮助他人的优秀学生。微软为他们提供最前沿的技术资源，以及更广泛的交流及展示自我的平台。 

九月开始，我们将分别邀请专注于不同技术领域的微软学生大使，针对时下备受关注的语言和技术，分享他们的学习方法与路径，帮助更多学生朋友更好地认识新技术，学习新语言，在技术的道路上走得更远。 

本期学生大使技能秀，我们将跟着学生大使的脚步，一起学习 .NET。 
作为一个免费、跨平台、开源的开发平台，.NET 在 Web 应用开发、微服务、移动和桌面应用、物联网、机器学习，以及云原生等多技术领域有着广泛的应用。今年更是 .NET 20周年，.NET 也即将迎来 .NET 7 的正式发布。未来，.NET 也将与时俱进，不断更新与完善，贡献到更多更前沿的技术领域中去，助力每一位 .NETer 的开发之路。 
20周年，.NET 一路走来，中国有许许多多的开发者与 .NET 一同成长直到今天。一个技术的发展需要不断的新鲜血液的加入，.NET 技术更是如此。本次学生大使技能秀，我们就来跟随新一代的 .NET 开发者，一同认识和学习开源 .NET。 
作为学生和初学者，我们为什么要选择 .NET？.NET 可以为我们的开发带来哪些快捷和便利？我们可以用 .NET 来做些什么？我们又可以怎样更快上手和掌握 .NET 开发呢？ 
听听学生大使候选人袁诗琪同学，为我们分享她的 .NET 之路。

title: MS Learn 学堂｜Rust 编程语言 - Rust 网络编程&IoT编程
description:

Rust 是近几年较“火”的一门新兴编程语言，它可以搭建传统命令行应用、Web 应用，以及 IoT 设备、网络服务器等，是一门全面创新的、可以进行底层开发的高级语言。 

你知道 Rust 吗？你想要了解或学习 Rust 编程语言吗？ 

很多开发者会觉得 Rust “难学”，诚然，Rust 在编译器级别有着严格的限制，这赋予了它高安全性，同时也带来了较高的学习门槛。 

然而，Rust 高性能、高可靠性、高生产力的特点，以及它不断更新中的新特性，也在吸引着更多的开发者学习和使用。 

那么，Rust 究竟是一门怎样的编程语言？它到底有多“难”？我们又该如何学习并使用 Rust 呢？ 

本月 MS Learn 学堂，就让我们一起来探究 Rust 编程语言。我们会通过3周的课程，为大家讲解 Rust 及其相关应用场景。希望这三期课程，可以帮助大家对 Rust 编程语言及其使用有更清晰的了解，更扎实地迈出使用 Rust 的第一步。

description:
